question: A son's present age is two-fifths of the age of his father. After 8 years from now, his age will be one-half of the age of his father. How old (in years) is the father at present?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio now (son : father) = 2 : 5

After 8 years → (2x + 8) : (5x + 8) = 1 : 2

Cross multiply → 2(2x + 8) = 5x + 8

4x + 16 = 5x + 8 → x = 8

**∴ Father’s age = 5x = 40 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Son’s age = 2/5 of father’s age

After 8 years, son’s age = 1/2 of father’s age

**Formula used:**

Form linear equations based on age relations

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let father’s present age = F

⇒ Son’s present age = (2/5)F

⇒ After 8 years: Son = (2/5)F + 8, Father = F + 8

⇒ (2/5)F + 8 = (1/2)(F + 8)

⇒ Multiply both sides by 10

⇒ 4F + 80 = 5F + 40

⇒ 80 − 40 = 5F − 4F

⇒ F = 40

**∴ The father’s present age is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Ratio Concept

Ages can be assumed in ratio form to simplify equations.

Linear Equations

Age problems are solved by forming and solving linear equations.

Future Age Relation

Add same number of years to both persons.

Cross Multiplication

Useful method to solve proportional equations quickly.
